newsitem.title: USA: Restrictions remain on Houston Ship Channel.
newsitem.headline: Restrictions remain on Houston Ship Channel.

text.p: Shipping restrictions remained in effect on Friday along sections of the Houston Ship Channel following a barge accident a day earlier, the U.S. Coast Guard and shipping officials said.

Shipping was restricted to barges, tows and shallow-draft vessels with drafts of 12 feet or less between light 52 and light 56 until six large tanks swept off a barge on Thursday are found, Coast Guard spokesman Tim Carlin said.

Deep-draft tankers can still reach refineries in the Galveston and Texas City areas, he said, but there is no deep- draft traffic into the Port of Houston along the Ship Channel, the waterway linking Houston's refinery row with the Gulf of Mexico.
The tanks, including two measuring 38-feet in length and 11-feet in diameter and four smaller tanks, sank to the bottom of the channel with their loads of zinc bromide in the accident, he said.
"If any ship were to hit that, it would do some sizable damage," he said.

A U.S. Army Corps of Engineers side-sweep sonar vessel Friday morning was preparing to resume its search for the tanks, which fell overboard after the barge was hit by the wake of a passing ship on Thursday.
The search was halted overnight as a band of strong thunderstorms moved through the area.

The Houston ship channel pilots could not release the exact number of deep-draft ships delayed by the accident. "We don't have a lot (of ships) backed up, but I can't say how many. It's not a lot," a dispatcher said.
